item.text: {"question_id":"5B.7","answer":"During 2023, Mexico had substantial evaluation, monitoring, statistical, and audit capacity, but the supplied evidence does not show consistent presidential use of adverse findings or correction of failing programs. CONEVAL coordinated 173 mandated evaluations, disseminated 95% of evaluations, reported completion of 95% of recorded improvement commitments, produced poverty and social-rights indicators, and documented several audits and corrective follow-up actions within CONEVAL itself (BATCH-0006-E003; BATCH-0013-E007; BATCH-0054-E007; BATCH-0054-E008). The federal administration also published more detailed poverty, geospatial, and planned-versus-executed resource information for 2023 planning (BATCH-0012-E003). These demonstrate available evidence and some institutional correction, but not that López Obrador personally adopted CONEVAL recommendations or that broader programs improved as a result. Contrary evidence is substantial and directly relevant to 2023: CONEVAL reported that monitoring recommendations had been disregarded to varying degrees; only 69% of 16 priority programs had result-oriented purposes, half measured results adequately, four required indicator adjustment, and four did not measure results. One program worsened in results orientation while others showed mixed design changes (BATCH-0052-E004; BATCH-0052-E006). The World Bank recorded closures, partial cancellations, dropped projects, unsigned loans, changing priorities, budget constraints, turnover, procurement delays, and limited implementation capacity during FY2020–2023, alongside some proactive restructurings and adjustments (BATCH-0052-E020). Independent reporting also described weakened transparency and access to information in 2023, including INAI paralysis after López Obrador vetoed appointments and coalition legislators rejected another proposal (BATCH-0009-E011; BATCH-0047-E013). In the corruption record, reports state that Segalmex irregularities were flagged from 2019 and accumulated before López Obrador acknowledged the diversion in December 2023 while describing it as the only corruption case in his government; the broader case count and selective-protection interpretation remain source-attributed and not fully adjudicated (BATCH-0006-E007; BATCH-0026-E003). A 2022 fact-checking record and 2022 reporting on presidential pressure toward Banxico are carryover context, not 2023 outcome evidence (BATCH-0042-E009; BATCH-0048-E003). Overall, the record supports functioning evaluation and audit institutions plus some documented corrections, but also weak results orientation, disregarded monitoring recommendations, implementation failures, restricted independent scrutiny, and evidence of denial or minimization. Attribution is strong for presidential statements, INAI-related actions, and transparency posture; it is weaker for agency-level data deficiencies, program design failures, and World Bank portfolio
